about: The stack policy (F3 item P; body B3, E2 policy layer): each rule written once as data. bin/policy.py renders it into each worker CLI's own permission config (the shapes in .stella/adapters.json), checks it, and catches a hand edit of a generated file (drift). The read guards (secret-guard.py, read-only-terminal.py), bin/box.py and git-guard.py read their rule through the one loader in bin/roles.py and fail closed when it cannot be read. A value that names another file (role_table#/...) is read there, never copied. {worktree} is the run's worktree.

rules.about: a worker writes only inside its worktree
the stack's protected paths (repo list anchored at the stack root, home list under each home) and the owner settings files are neither read nor written by a worker CLI

deny: file name globs (no slash) and home globs (~/); allow: names that are never secret; dirs: folders a recursive search must not enter (a ~/ folder under each home); text: regular expressions a command line must not name (a match whose word is an allowed name is let through); glob_probes: names a dotted glob is tried against

deny_git.why: git add -A/--all/. sweeps unrelated files; add files by name

rules.about: git words a worker never runs, each with why (the refusal's text): global (an option before the subcommand), sub (a subcommand), option (an option anywhere), sub_args (a subcommand's argument; a one-letter option also inside a group such as -an). Commits go only to the worker's own card worktree (git-guard.py, bin/commit-guard.sh)
a board action whose flag no role of an adapter's worker profiles holds is denied to that CLI's shell
a worker CLI runs only the model the resolver assigns; each adapter's model_flags (adapters.json) name the flags that pick another model or skip permissions, denied in every CLI's shell

sandbox.about: The worker CLI's tool subprocesses: credential folders hidden, the worktree the only writable path, network only through the egress proxy. Data only until E1 enforces it (features.json stub adapter-sandbox).
